description:
Two distinct interner arena slots hold MUTUALLY-SUBTYPE (i.e. equal) types.
Interning is supposed to give one identity per type; here one type has two.

## Measured

`00420_enum_take_drop_split`, release. Temporary probe: dump `(id, display)` for
all 1,424 arena slots, then for every same-display pair ask the compiler's own
`is_subtype` in both directions.

    EQUIV  1006  1008  axes_differing=[tuples(len 2 vs 2),
                                       tuples_are_permutation_of_each_other=false]
    EQUIV  1007  1009  axes_differing=[tuples(len 2 vs 2),
                                       tuples_are_permutation_of_each_other=false]

Both pairs are mutually subtype, display identically
(`{[int], []} | {[], [int]}` and its `{:cont, ...}` wrapper), and differ only on
the `tuples` axis with equal clause counts.

## Why it happens

`Descr` derives structural `PartialEq`/`Eq`/`Hash` (`types/descr.rs:28`) over
`tuples: Vec<Conj<TupleSig>>`, and `TypeInterner::intern` (`types/mod.rs:125`)
dedupes on that structural equality. Structural equality is strictly FINER than
type equivalence, so two decompositions of one union take two slots.

`canonicalize_tuple_axis` (`types/mod.rs:226`) is the intended closer and does
not close it: it drops provably-empty clauses and absorbs subsumed ones, then
`out.push(c)` preserves whatever decomposition arrived.

## Mechanism narrowed, not yet pinned -- start here

RULED OUT: clause ordering (`[A,B]` vs `[B,A]`). `types/format.rs` contains no
sort, so display renders stored order; both slots display identically, AND the
probe reports the clause lists are not permutations of each other. Do not
re-derive this.

REMAINING HYPOTHESIS: two different clause decompositions of one union -- most
likely a redundant or vacuous negative factor in a surviving `Conj`, which
display does not render. Pinning which is task one.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Two `Ty` ids for one type means any memo, dedup, or spec key that hashes on `Ty`
MISSES. Against this tree's live over-specialization work (fz-y6w collapsed
quicksort 35 -> 24 specs) that is a correctness-and-cost concern, not a cosmetic
one. Check whether SpecKey/activation keying is currently splitting on it.

It is ALSO one of four clusters behind run-to-run `Ty` renumbering: whichever
decomposition is built first takes the lower slot. Fixing this removes that
cluster. The other three clusters are genuine upstream mint-order dependence and
are NOT this ticket -- see fz-kdt.47.

## Checks

- A test asserts no two arena slots are mutually subtype, over the full arena of
  both target fixtures.
- The two pairs above collapse to one id each.
- Existing type tests (`types_test.rs`, incl. `union_absorbs_subsumed_tuple_clauses`)
  stay green.
- The permanent ratchet is fz-f98.21's faithful `canon`: `canon(a) == canon(b)
  && a != b`. This ticket does not depend on f98.21 to be FIXED, only to be
  permanently guarded.
title: Interner holds two identities for one type: Descr equality is finer than type equivalence
